prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: use a local-knowledge management service (my top pick is Yext) combined with manual testing in the major AI assistants (ChatGPT/GPT with browsing, Google Bard/SGE, Bing Chat, Siri, Alexa). Yext gives you the most direct control over what AI/search assistants see; BrightLocal or Moz Local are great, cheaper monitoring alternatives.

Why Yext (and similar services) is best
- Yext lets you create a canonical “knowledge graph” for your business (name, address, hours, products, FAQs, photos) and pushes that authoritative data to Google, Apple, Bing, Yelp, Facebook, voice assistants and many directories.  
- Many AI assistants and search models draw on those same directories or the Knowledge Graph data, so controlling those sources makes it much more likely an AI will recommend you accurately.  
- Yext also provides analytics so you can see where your business appears and how often it’s surfaced.

Other important services to use
- Google Business Profile (mandatory) — the single most important listing for Google Search, Maps and Google Assistant/Bard/SGE.  
- Apple Business Connect — influences Siri/Apple Maps.  
- Bing Places — influences Bing Chat and Microsoft products.  
- Yelp and Facebook — commonly used by voice assistants and recommendation engines.  
- BrightLocal, Moz Local, or Whitespark — for citation monitoring, rank tracking and reputation management if you prefer a lower-cost option than Yext.  
- Data aggregators (Infogroup, Neustar, Factual) — register to improve directory reach.

Technical items that make AIs more likely to recommend you
- Schema.org LocalBusiness structured data on your site (NAP, hours, services, reviews).  
- High-quality, crawlable website and clear service/location pages.  
- Consistent NAP (name, address, phone) and identical hours across listings.  
- Positive reviews on Google, Yelp, Facebook — many AIs surface or weigh review sources.  
- Wikipedia / Wikidata / local business directories if applicable — used by some assistants for knowledge panels.

How to test whether AIs recommend your business
1. Query the assistants directly:  
   - Google/Bard (or Google Search + SGE): “best [service] near [city/zip]” or “best [service] near me” (from your location).  
   - ChatGPT with browsing (or GPT-4o/GPT-4 with live web access): same prompts plus “Recommend 3 [service type] in [city]” and include your business name.  
   - Bing Chat, Siri, Alexa: similar natural queries; try voice and text variants.  
2. Test prompts that look for authoritative sources: “Which businesses match [business name] at [address]?” or “Give top 3 [service] within X miles of [address].”  
3. Track over time after you update listings to see whether AI outputs change.  
4. Use monitoring tools (BrightLocal, Yext) to see citation coverage and local rank improvements.

Notes about ChatGPT specifically
- Out-of-the-box ChatGPT (no browsing) answers from training data and may not reliably recommend small, new, or local businesses. With browsing or live web access, it will use web sources — so controlling those sources matters.  
- You can also create a ChatGPT plugin or supply a knowledge base (if you want enterprise-level control over how a hosted AI recommends you), but that’s more complex.

Recommended immediate action plan (quick)
1. Claim and optimize Google Business Profile.  
2. Sign up for Yext (or BrightLocal if you want a lower-cost option) and sync your listings.  
3. Add schema markup and location/service pages on your website.  
4. Solicit and respond to reviews.  
5. Test ChatGPT, Bard, Bing Chat, Siri and Alexa with the example prompts above and track changes.

If you want, tell me:
- your business type and city and I’ll give exact prompt examples you can use for ChatGPT, Bard and Siri, and suggest which listing to prioritize.
